climate.overview_html: The dominant new climate signal on September 4 is the World Meteorological Organization’s September 3 warning that the developing Super El Niño could become the strongest since instrumental monitoring began, with WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo stating it may be “literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades” and assigning a nearly 100% probability that El Niño will persist through February 2027 — the highest certainty WMO has ever expressed in any El Niño update; climate scientist Daniel Swain estimates a ~70% likelihood this event will surpass the 2015–16 “Super El Niño” and that 2027 has the potential to become the warmest year on record as oceanic heat releases slowly into the atmosphere after the peak. European wildfires and drought continue as a co-dominant story: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area has now reached 647,375 hectares, with very extreme fire danger forecast across a broad band from Iberia through France, the Alps, the Balkans, Greece, Turkey and Ukraine through September 9 — extending the previously flagged September 5 deadline by four days and confirming the atmospheric blocking pattern has strengthened rather than broken. The Nepal–Tibet glacier collapse disaster is directly amplified by the same El Niño thermodynamics: the death toll has risen to more than 1,100 and the number unaccounted-for to approximately 4,500 as of September 4, and Chinese state media warns that glaciers surrounding the impact crater “may still collapse, posing significant potential risks.”

items.source: WMO / Al Jazeera / phys.org / US News
items.headline: WMO September 3 Warning: Super El Niño Could Be “Off the Charts” — Strongest Since Monitoring Began; Nearly 100% Probability El Niño Persists Through February; WMO SG Saulo Issues Unprecedented Alert; 2027 Could Be Warmest Year on Record
items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization issued an unprecedented El Niño warning on September 3, stating that the developing event could become the strongest since systematic monitoring began in the mid-20th century. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said: 'If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began. So literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades.' WMO's September update assigns nearly 100% probability — the highest certainty it has ever expressed in an El Niño/La Niña advisory — that El Niño will continue through at least February 2027. Climate scientist Daniel Swain (UCLA) estimates a ~70% probability this event will exceed the 2015–16 peak, which currently ranks as the strongest on the multi-variate ENSO index. The most alarming longer-range implication: because ocean heat releases into the atmosphere on a lagged timescale, the peak atmospheric warming driven by this El Niño will arrive in 2027 — meaning 2027 has the potential to become the warmest year on record even if ocean temperatures begin declining in early 2027. The WMO forecast is consistent with NOAA CPC's August ENSO Diagnostic assigning >90% probability of a very strong event during September–November 2026.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: 647,375 Hectares Burned — Very Extreme Fire Danger Forecast Through September 9 Across Iberia, France, Alps, Balkans, Greece, Turkey, Ukraine; Blocking Pattern Strengthened; Rhine and Danube at Record-Low Stages; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area of 647,375 hectares as of the September 3–4 update, an increase from the 634,473 hectares reported on August 30 and still tracking significantly ahead of the same date in the 2025 record season. Very extreme fire danger is now forecast through September 9 — four days beyond the September 5 endpoint previously flagged — across a broad geographic arc running from Iberia and France through the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The extension reflects a strengthened and persistent atmospheric blocking pattern rather than the anticipated breakdown. The Rhine remains at its lowest level since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest continues at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances. The 2026 European wildfire and drought emergency, corroborated by WWA attribution research, represents the direct physical signal of anthropogenic warming operating through the lens of a Super El Niño baseline.

items.headline: Climate Change Is Now Europe’s Biggest Systemic Security Threat — 10,000 Excess Deaths From June Heatwave; 9M Tonnes Crop Loss; Military Assets Diverted to Fire Suppression and Flood Defense
items.summary: Chatham House published a policy analysis concluding that climate change is now Europe's biggest systemic security risk. The summer of 2026 provides the evidence base: extreme heat contributed to an estimated 10,000 excess deaths during the June heatwave alone and destroyed approximately 9 million tonnes of crops. The security dimension is direct: Europe's armed forces are increasingly deployed to fight fires, reinforce flood defenses, evacuate populations, and restore critical infrastructure — diverting capacity from conventional security operations. Rhine water levels fell to their lowest since 1880. Chatham House argues that climate adaptation investment has structurally lagged behind mitigation spending and that European security planning must treat climate hazard as a primary threat category.

items.headline: NOAA August ENSO Diagnostic: Niño 3.4 Reaches +2.7°C Week of August 12; All 15 Ensemble Members Forecast Peak >+2.5°C; >90% Probability “Very Strong” Event Sept–Nov 2026; No La Niña Transition Before Spring 2027
items.summary: NOAA CPC's August 2026 ENSO Diagnostic Discussion confirms the ongoing El Niño is now tracking toward historically extreme territory. The Niño 3.4 sea surface temperature anomaly index reached +2.03°C in July 2026 and +2.7°C in the week centered on August 12 — already exceeding the +2.5°C threshold for a 'very strong' event. All 15 coupled model ensemble members in the multi-model objective ENSO outlook forecast Niño 3.4 exceeding +2.5°C at the September–November peak window; a majority project exceedance of +3.0°C, which would formally qualify this as a 'Super El Niño' comparable to the 2015–16 event. NOAA assigns greater than 90% probability to a very strong event during September–November 2026 with little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027. The September 3 WMO update reinforces this with even higher certainty language.

items.source: CBC News / Al Jazeera / ICIMOD / CNN
items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: Death Toll Rises to 1,100+; 4,500+ Now Missing or Unaccounted-For; Chinese State Media Warns More Glacial Collapses Possible; ICIMOD HKH Outlook 2026 Documents 12% Glacial Area Loss
items.summary: The August 27 glacial collapse at Nepal's border with China's Tibet Autonomous Region continues to evolve: the confirmed death toll has risen to more than 1,100 across both countries as of September 4, and the number of people missing or unaccounted-for has grown to approximately 4,500 — up from the 1,000 dead and 3,000 missing reported on September 1. Chinese state media warns that glaciers surrounding the impact crater 'may still collapse, posing significant potential risks.' The disaster is framed by ICIMOD's HKH Glacier Outlook 2026, which documents a 12% loss of glacial area in the Hindu Kush Himalayan region between 1990 and 2020. Scientists directly link the accelerating instability to Super El Niño-driven baseline ocean and atmospheric warming amplifying decadal glacier mass loss.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lowell (Central Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Weakened to Category 4 (140 mph); Sharp North Turn Expected Saturday; Forecast Track West of Kauai Tuesday; Still Major Hurricane Threat to Hawaiian Islands; CPHC: “Too Soon to Determine Potential Impacts”
major_events.status: CATEGORY 4 · 140 MPH · SHARP NORTH TURN EXPECTED SAT · WEST OF KAUAI FORECAST TUESDAY · MAJOR HURRICANE THREAT ISLANDS
major_events.impact: Hurricane Lowell weakened slightly from its historic Category 5 peak (160 mph) to Category 4 status with maximum sustained winds near 140 mph as of September 3 advisories — consistent with the CPHC noting some erosion of the warm core. The track forecast has, however, moved more alarming: CPHC now projects a sharp turn to the north beginning Saturday into Sunday, with the center forecast to pass west of Kauai early Tuesday still at or near major hurricane strength. Long-range model guidance has progressively converged toward a track closer to the island chain, with some ensemble members placing the center dangerously near Kauai. CPHC stated it is still 'too soon to determine potential impacts in the Hawaiian Islands,' reflecting high track and intensity uncertainty. Life-threatening surf and rip currents are already increasing across the island chain. Honolulu Mayor Rick Blangiardi's preparedness guidance remains in effect. The situation remains an extremely serious and rapidly evolving threat environment for Hawaii, Maui, and the entire island chain.

major_events.name: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods — STATUS UPDATE: 1,100+ Dead, 4,500+ Missing; Chinese Authorities Warn of Additional Glacial Collapse Risk; Unstable Barrier Lake Threat Persists; 900+ Workers Still Unaccounted-For in Tunnels
major_events.status: 1,100+ DEAD · 4,500+ MISSING · ADDITIONAL COLLAPSE RISK WARNING · BARRIER LAKE THREAT · 900+ IN TUNNELS
major_events.impact: The death toll from the August 27 Nepal-Tibet glacial collapse flood has risen to more than 1,100 people across both countries as of September 4, with approximately 4,500 now missing or unaccounted-for — up from 1,000+ dead and 3,000+ missing in the September 1 count. Chinese state media has issued a warning that glaciers surrounding the impact crater 'may still collapse, posing significant potential risks.' The newly-formed unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border continues to threaten a secondary catastrophic flood event, and at least 900 workers remain unaccounted-for inside flooded or buried hydropower tunnels. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police personnel continue search-and-rescue operations, with helicopter supply runs to cut-off communities. Officials warn the death toll is likely to rise as teams reach previously inaccessible areas.

major_events.name: Hurricane Karina (Eastern Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Weakening; Forecast Post-Tropical by Monday; No Hawaii Threat; Drier Air and Cooler Waters Taking Toll
major_events.status: WEAKENING CATEGORY 4 · FORECAST POST-TROPICAL MON · NO HAWAII THREAT · DISSIPATING
major_events.impact: Hurricane Karina's threat posture has changed significantly: the environment surrounding Karina has become increasingly hostile with drier air, lower sea surface temperatures, and rising vertical wind shear. NHC now forecasts Karina to become a post-tropical system by Monday before dissipating, with no threat to Hawaii at this time. This eliminates the dramatic dual-major-hurricane Hawaii convergence scenario that was elevated as of September 2–3. Karina's weakening removes one critical variable from the Hawaii threat assessment, but Lowell's track remains the dominant concern.

major_events.name: Hurricane Marie (Eastern Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Upgraded From Tropical Storm to Hurricane (80 mph); Third Named Pacific System; No Landfall Forecast
major_events.status: HURRICANE · 80 MPH · UPGRADED FROM TROPICAL STORM · NO LANDFALL
major_events.impact: Tropical Storm Marie was upgraded to hurricane status with maximum sustained winds near 80 mph — a status change from September 3's tropical storm designation of 45 mph. Marie continues developing off the southwestern coast of Mexico. No landfall is forecast. Marie's upgrade to hurricane status maintains three simultaneous named storms in the Pacific, though with Karina now forecast to dissipate, the dual-major-hurricane Hawaii threat window has closed. Marie is not expected to affect land areas.

major_events.name: Indonesia / SE Asia / Philippines Wildfire Haze — ASEAN Level 3 and Red Haze Alert Active; Metro Manila PM2.5 Acutely Unhealthy; 600+ Malaysian Schools Closed; Habagat Transport Ongoing; Dry Season Expected to Persist
major_events.status: ASEAN LEVEL 3 · RED HAZE ALERT · ACUTELY UNHEALTHY MANILA · 600+ SCHOOLS CLOSED MALAYSIA · DRY SEASON RISK THROUGH MID-SEPT
major_events.impact: Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Brunei face a rare Red haze alert as Kalimantan fires transported by the southwest monsoon (Habagat) continue blanketing Southeast Asia. Metro Manila PM2.5 readings remain at acutely unhealthy levels across multiple stations. Over 600 schools in Malaysia's Sarawak remain closed. The ASEAN Specialized Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert remains active. Indonesia's burned area has grown roughly 2.5x since February 2026 as El Niño conditions intensify, and ASEAN's regional seasonal outlook predicts below-normal rainfall for much of the region through early October — sustaining fire risk well into mid-September.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — 299 Dead Including 140 Children; NDMA: 2–3 More Monsoon Spells in September; Flash Flood Risk Across All Provinces
major_events.status: ONGOING · 299 DEAD · 140 CHILDREN · PEAK MONSOON · 2–3 MORE SPELLS FORECAST
major_events.impact: Pakistan's cumulative monsoon season death toll stands at 299, including 140 children, 102 men, and 57 women, per the most recent NDMA reporting. An additional 715 people have been injured. Property damage has affected 1,676 homes, with 562 completely destroyed. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa leads in provincial fatalities, followed by Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan, AJK, and Gilgit-Baltistan. NDMA forecasts 2–3 additional monsoon pulse events during September — the climatological peak. This season's rainfall is running 50–60% heavier than the comparable period last year.

major_events.name: Europe Wildfire and Drought Emergency — 647,375 ha Burned; Very Extreme Fire Danger Extended Through September 9; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Danube Record Low; Paks Nuclear Output Curtailed
major_events.status: ONGOING · 647,375 HA · VERY EXTREME FIRE DANGER THROUGH SEPT 9 · RHINE LOWEST SINCE 1880 · PAKS CURTAILED
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area at 647,375 hectares — a 13,000-hectare increase from August 30. The very extreme fire danger window has been extended from September 5 to September 9, covering Iberia, France, the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The atmospheric blocking pattern responsible for Europe's exceptional heat and drought has strengthened rather than weakened. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — HELD Status Maintained; ~25,163 Hectares; Phased Re-Entry Assessment Ongoing; 379 Firefighters Active
major_events.status: HELD · ~25,163 HA · PHASED RE-ENTRY · 379 FIREFIGHTERS ACTIVE
major_events.impact: BC Wildfire Service's HELD classification for the Bald Range wildfire near Summerland is maintained. The fire has burned approximately 25,163 hectares. 379 wildland firefighters, 7 helicopters, and 43 pieces of heavy equipment remain assigned. Evacuation orders and alerts remain active for portions of Summerland and Peachland. A phased re-entry assessment continues for lower-risk zones. The fire has damaged or destroyed approximately 150 structures and claimed one life. Cooler weather and rainfall since August 28 have aided suppression.

weather.overview_html: The pivotal shift in the Pacific hurricane situation on September 4 is Hurricane Lowell’s slight weakening from Category 5 to Category 4 (140 mph), paired with a track forecast that has moved closer to the Hawaiian Islands — with CPHC now projecting a sharp northward turn beginning Saturday and the center passing west of Kauai early Tuesday still at or near major hurricane strength, while CPHC cautioned it is “too soon to determine potential impacts in the Hawaiian Islands”. Simultaneously, Hurricane Karina is now forecast to become post-tropical by Monday with no Hawaii threat, significantly reducing the dual-hurricane convergence scenario, while Tropical Storm Marie has been upgraded to hurricane status with 80 mph winds. In South Asia, the Nepal–Tibet death toll has risen to more than 1,100 with approximately 4,500 now missing, and Chinese authorities have warned that additional glacial collapses remain possible. Southeast Asia continues under a rare Red haze alert with metro Manila PM2.5 at acutely unhealthy levels and over 600 Malaysian schools closed, while European wildfires reach 647,375 hectares with very extreme fire danger now extending through September 9.

items.source: Hawaii News Now / Kauai Now / CPHC
items.headline: Hurricane Lowell Weakens to Category 4 (140 mph); Track Forecast Edges Closer to Hawaiian Islands; Sharp North Turn Expected Saturday; CPHC: West of Kauai Tuesday; Forecast Still at Major Hurricane Strength at Closest Approach
items.summary: Hurricane Lowell weakened slightly to Category 4 status with maximum sustained winds near 140 mph as of September 3 advisories, down from its historic Category 5 peak of 160 mph. While the intensity step-down provides marginal relief, the track forecast has become more alarming: CPHC now projects a sharp right turn beginning Saturday into Sunday, with the center forecast to pass west of Kauai early Tuesday at or near major hurricane strength. Long-range model guidance has progressively converged toward a track closer to the Hawaiian Islands, with some ensemble members placing the center within dangerous proximity to Kauai. CPHC stated that it is still 'too soon to determine potential impacts in the Hawaiian Islands,' reflecting substantial track uncertainty over the critical turn timing. Life-threatening surf and rip current conditions are already increasing across the islands. All Hawaii residents are urged to continue preparations.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Death Toll Rises to 1,100+; Missing Now ~4,500; Chinese Authorities Warn Additional Glacial Collapses Possible; 5,000+ Rescue Workers Active; Inaccessible Areas Still Not Reached
items.summary: The death toll from the August 27 Nepal-Tibet glacial collapse disaster has risen to more than 1,100 as of September 4, with the number of people missing or unaccounted-for growing to approximately 4,500 — up from 1,000+ dead and 3,000+ missing in September 1 counts. Chinese state media issued a warning that glaciers surrounding the impact crater 'may still collapse, posing significant potential risks,' maintaining acute secondary disaster risk. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police personnel are conducting search operations; helicopters are delivering emergency supplies to cut-off communities. The unstable barrier lake straddling the Nepal-China border continues to threaten a secondary catastrophic flood. Officials warn the death toll will likely rise further as teams reach previously inaccessible areas. Satellite imagery continues to show an altered river course and multiple landslide-dammed impoundments.

items.headline: Hurricane Karina Now Forecast Post-Tropical by Monday, No Hawaii Threat; Marie Upgraded to Hurricane (80 mph) — Pacific Basin Still Has Two Active Storms Under Super El Niño
items.summary: Hurricane Karina's situation has shifted substantially: drier air intrusion, lower sea surface temperatures, and increasing vertical wind shear are now expected to cause rapid deterioration, with NHC forecasting Karina to become post-tropical by Monday before dissipating. No threat to Hawaii is forecast. This eliminates the dramatic dual-major-hurricane convergence scenario centered on the Hawaiian Islands. Separately, Tropical Storm Marie has been upgraded to hurricane status with maximum sustained winds near 80 mph off the Mexican coast — the storm's third named-system designation in the basin. No landfall is forecast for Marie. The basin still contains two active systems (Lowell and Marie) under Super El Niño sea surface temperatures, maintaining the extraordinary Pacific season context.

items.headline: Toxic Wildfire Haze Spreads Across SE Asia as Super El Niño Intensifies; Red Haze Alert Active; Philippines, Malaysia Schools Closed; Below-Normal Rainfall Expected Through Early October; Indonesia Burned Area Up 2.5x Since February
items.summary: A rare Red haze alert is active across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Brunei as Kalimantan wildfire smoke transported by the southwest monsoon blankets much of Southeast Asia. Indonesia's burned area has grown roughly 2.5x between February and May 2026 (from 32,637 to ~81,000 hectares) as El Niño conditions intensify, and fire risk is expected to remain elevated. The ASEAN regional seasonal outlook predicts below-normal rainfall for most of the region through early October, sustaining fire conditions. Schools in Malaysia's Sarawak and the Philippines remain closed; Metro Manila PM2.5 readings remain at acutely unhealthy levels. The ASEAN Specialized Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert continues.

items.headline: Pakistan Monsoon Death Toll at 299 Including 140 Children; 715 Injured; NDMA Warns 2–3 More Monsoon Spells in September; Season Running 50–60% Heavier Than Last Year
items.summary: Pakistan's cumulative monsoon season death toll stands at 299, including 140 children, 102 men, and 57 women, per NDMA reporting. An additional 715 people have been injured (239 children). Property damage has affected 1,676 homes, with 562 completely destroyed. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa leads in provincial fatalities, followed by Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan, AJK, and Gilgit-Baltistan. NDMA forecasts 2–3 additional monsoon pulse events during September — the climatological peak — with flash-flood and heavy-rain advisories continuing across all affected provinces. This season's rainfall is running 50–60% heavier than the comparable period last year.

renewables.overview_html: The headline new project milestone is RWE and TotalEnergies’ OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) installing its first of 53 monopiles on September 1 in the North Sea 53 km west of IJmuiden — beginning construction of the 795 MW project that will use Vestas V236-15 MW turbines and, once operational in early 2028, supply the equivalent of 1 million Dutch households. In the US structural story, EIA data show solar, wind, and storage added 44,889 MW in the year to June 2026 versus only 7,530 MW for natural gas, with combined renewable installed capacity on pace to surpass the entire gas fleet within approximately 12 months, and solar led US monthly generation for the first time ever in June 2026 while wind and solar combined delivered a record 22.3% of H1 US electrical production. The federal–state collision continues: California’s lawsuit over the Trump administration’s $120 million buyout of the 2 GW Golden State Wind lease proceeds, while in the UK, plug-in residential solar panels became legal from August 27 under SI 2026/848 and are now available at 800+ Argos stores.

items.headline: OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) First Monopile Installed — 795 MW RWE/TotalEnergies JV; 53 Vestas V236-15 MW Turbines; 53 km Off Dutch Coast; 1 Million Dutch Households by 2028; Innovative Transition-Piece-Less Design
items.summary: The offshore installation vessel Les Alizés successfully installed the first of 53 monopiles for the OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) offshore wind farm on September 1. The 795 MW project is a joint venture between RWE and TotalEnergies, located 53 km west of IJmuiden in the Dutch North Sea. The wind farm will use 53 Vestas V236-15 MW turbines — some of the largest offshore turbines commercially deployed. The project uses innovative transition-piece-less monopiles, where turbine towers are bolted directly to the monopile without a transition piece, reducing steel requirements per foundation. Installation of all 53 monopiles is expected to complete by early 2027; inter-array cable installation is scheduled for late 2026 and turbine installation in 2027, with the farm fully operational by early 2028. When operational, OranjeWind will supply the equivalent of approximately 1 million Dutch households.

items.headline: Victoria Launches Australia’s First Offshore Wind Auction: 2 GW Tendered Across Bass Strait and Southern Ocean Zones; 12-Month RFP Phase; Contracts Expected 2028; Pathway to 9 GW by 2040
items.summary: Victoria launched Australia's first offshore wind auction on August 25–26, opening a 12-month Request for Proposal phase for projects to deliver 2 GW of offshore wind generation. The auction covers two declared offshore wind zones in the Bass Strait off Gippsland and the Southern Ocean off western Victoria. Contracts for the first 2 GW are expected to be awarded in 2028. The 2 GW round is the first step toward Victoria's 4 GW by 2035 and 9 GW by 2040 targets. Successful projects would generate electricity for approximately 1.5 million homes. The auction confirms Australia is operationalizing offshore wind policy after years of legislative development.

items.headline: California Sues Trump Administration Over $120 Million Deal to Cancel 2 GW Golden State Wind Offshore Lease; Alleges Violations of Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act; $100M in Port/Transmission Prep Already Spent
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta and the California Energy Commission filed suit August 28 against the Trump administration and Golden State Wind, challenging the Interior Department's agreement to pay $120 million to abandon its 2 GW offshore wind lease and invest instead in fossil fuel projects. The complaint alleges violations of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, the Judgment Fund Act, and other federal statutes. The 2 GW project would have supplied clean electricity to more than 1 million California homes. The state notes it has already spent more than $100 million on port upgrades, transmission improvements, and other infrastructure in preparation for the project.

items.headline: EIA Data: US Renewables Installed Capacity to Surpass Natural Gas Within 12 Months — Solar+Wind Added 44,889 MW vs. Gas’s 7,530 MW in Year to June 2026; Battery Storage Up 17,859 MW
items.summary: New EIA capacity data show US renewable energy installed capacity is on pace to surpass natural gas within approximately 12 months — most likely by summer 2027. In the year through June 30, 2026: utility-scale solar added 28,077 MW; small-scale solar added 6,492 MW; wind added 10,553 MW; combined renewable additions totaled 44,889 MW. Natural gas capacity grew by only 7,530 MW in the same period. Utility-scale battery storage added 17,859 MW. When combined renewables capacity eventually exceeds natural gas's installed base, it will mark a structural inflection in the US power system.

items.headline: Solar Leads US Monthly Generation for First Time Ever in June 2026; 22.3% of H1 US Production From Wind+Solar; Renewable Buildout Outpacing Federal Headwinds
items.summary: CleanTechnica's analysis of EIA data finds that solar-generated electricity exceeded both wind and hydropower output for the month of June 2026 — the first time solar ranked as the leading renewable source for any calendar month in US history. Combined solar and wind provided 22.3% of domestic electrical production in H1 2026. Between July 2025 and June 2026: utility-scale solar grew 28,076.7 MW; small-scale solar added 6,492 MW; wind grew 10,552.9 MW. The analysis frames federal headwinds as causing friction at the margins rather than reversing structural momentum.

items.headline: UK Plug-In Solar Panels Legal Across Great Britain From August 27 — SI 2026/848 Enables 800 W Residential Systems Via Standard Sockets; Available at 800+ Argos Stores; Saves Up to £110/Year
items.summary: Plug-in solar panels became legal for residential use across England, Wales, and Scotland from August 27, 2026, under Plug-In Solar Amendment SI 2026/848. The regulation allows compliant systems with a maximum rated AC output of 800 W to connect via an approved standard plug without planning permission or a certified electrician. The change creates a legal pathway similar to Germany, France, and the Netherlands. Systems are immediately available at over 800 Argos stores and are estimated to save households up to £110 per year.

science.overview_html: The landmark development on September 3 is Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582), the first global AI weather model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — achieving hourly forecast updates at up to 5 km surface resolution, 60% improved precipitation evaluation against IMERG versus WeatherNext 2, explicit 100-meter wind-height forecasts for wind-turbine applications, and ranking first on Brightband’s Operational WeatherBench comparison; the model is already live in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, and available to researchers via BigQuery, Earth Engine, and Cloud Storage. Also new in the rolling window: arXiv:2609.00847 (September 1, Barcelona Supercomputing Center / ECML PKDD GREEN-AI workshop) presents the first comprehensive checklist for assessing and reducing the energy and carbon footprint of ML/AI applications across the full Earth System Modeling pipeline. Carried forward from the window: arXiv 2608.30795’s probabilistic Aardvark Weather, which finds that uncertainty decomposition improves mean-forecast skill by 4.2%; the GRL study detecting 245 glacial-earthquake events at Thwaites with the 2018–2020 cluster coinciding with episodic glacier acceleration — directly relevant as the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster evolves; and ECMWF’s operationally deployed AIFL LSTM, detecting 20-year flood signals six days in advance.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind Launches Hourly 5-km Global AI Weather Model; Trains on Raw Observations; 60% Better Precipitation vs. WN2; 100-m Wind-Height Forecasts for Turbines; Tops Brightband WeatherBench; Now Live in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is Google DeepMind's most advanced global weather forecasting model, introduced September 3 via an arXiv paper and simultaneously deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, Maps Platform, BigQuery, Google Earth Engine, and Google Cloud Storage. The key architectural breakthrough: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and to train on raw weather station observations rather than reanalysis-only data — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based AI models and shrinking it to 3–4 hours with hourly forecast cycles. Resolution: 5 km for key surface variables (temperature, moisture), 10 km for other surface variables, 25 km for atmospheric variables, and explicit 100-meter hub-height wind forecasts for wind turbine power estimation alongside cloud cover and solar radiation for grid operators. WeatherNext 3 has 2.4x more parameters than WeatherNext 2. Precipitation evaluation shows CRPS improvements of up to 60% against IMERG and 50% Brier score reduction versus NWP baselines at early lead times. On Brightband's Operational WeatherBench — the community benchmark for operational head-to-head comparison — WeatherNext 3 ranks first across key variables including temperature, wind speed, and humidity. The model is immediately accessible via the Google Maps Platform Weather API and through BigQuery ML infrastructure for enterprise and research users.

items.source: arXiv / Barcelona Supercomputing Center / ECML PKDD 2026
items.headline: arXiv 2609.00847: First Comprehensive Checklist for Energy and Carbon Footprints of ML/AI in Earth System Modeling; Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Presented at GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026 Naples
items.meta: Dainelli, Mozaffari, Castaño et al. (BSC Earth Dept.) · arXiv:2609.00847 · September 1, 2026 · GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026, Naples
items.summary: As machine learning and AI find their way into nearly every aspect of climate, weather, and Earth system modeling, this Barcelona Supercomputing Center paper provides the first comprehensive checklist for ML/AI practitioners and Earth system scientists to assess and reduce the environmental footprint of their applications. The checklist is organized around successive stages of the model development pipeline — data curation, model architecture, training regime, inference, and deployment — and is complemented by a curated selection of metrics from the literature for estimating energy consumption and carbon footprint at each stage. The work is timely given the explosive growth of compute-intensive neural weather models (WeatherNext 3, Pangu, GraphCast, Aardvark et al.) and raises the question of whether the carbon cost of training and running these models is being systematically accounted for in the research community. Presented at the GREEN-AI workshop of ECML PKDD 2026 in Naples.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.30795: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting — Aardvark Weather Made Probabilistic; Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Decomposed; Probabilistic Fine-Tuning Improves Mean Forecast 4.2%
items.meta: Almeida, Otero, Arndt, Baur, Samek, Ma · arXiv:2608.30795 · Submitted 31 Aug 2026
items.summary: This paper renders the Aardvark Weather end-to-end AI weather system probabilistic by attaching two stochastic mechanisms: (1) learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder, capturing aleatoric uncertainty inherited from the observing system; and (2) Monte Carlo dropout in the processor, capturing epistemic uncertainty in learned atmospheric dynamics. A law-of-total-variance decomposition attributes forecast spread to each source. Key empirical result: probabilistic fine-tuning improves the mean forecast by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times — demonstrating that uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill are mutually reinforcing rather than in tension.

items.headline: GRL: 245 Glacial Earthquakes Detected at Thwaites “Doomsday Glacier” Marine Edge 2010–2023 — Busiest Cluster 2018–2020 Coincided With Episodic Glacier Acceleration; Signals Destabilizing Ice Dynamics
items.meta: Pham et al. (Australian National University) · Geophysical Research Letters · Published 29 Aug 2026
items.summary: A study published in Geophysical Research Letters presents the first systematic detection of 245 previously uncatalogued seismic events near Thwaites Glacier's marine edge, catalogued over 2010–2023. Most are likely glacial earthquakes caused by capsizing, calving icebergs colliding with the parent glacier. The 2018–2020 cluster was the busiest period, coinciding with episodic acceleration of Thwaites' floating ice tongue toward the sea as observed in satellite data — suggesting that changing ocean conditions destabilizing the ice simultaneously drive faster flow and more calving. The findings add seismic evidence to the broad body of research showing Thwaites' marine-based instability is accelerating, directly relevant as the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster underscores global glacial hazard.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.26822 (Nested-EAGLE): Single ML System Bridges 0.25° Global and 6-km Regional Forecasting Over CONUS; Lower MSE Than Both GFS and HRRR for Near-Surface Fields
items.summary: A NOAA team introduces Nested-EAGLE, an ML weather prediction system that unifies short-range and medium-range forecasting in a single architecture — combining a 0.25° global forecast model with a 6 km refinement over CONUS. Nested-EAGLE achieves significantly lower mean-squared error in near-surface and low-level quantities over CONUS compared to both GFS and HRRR, while remaining competitive globally. The authors argue this unified short-and-medium-range system would provide the public with an improved distillation of global weather and local impacts.

items.headline: ECMWF Operationally Deploys AIFL: LSTM Global Streamflow Model Trained on 18,588 Basins; Detects 20-Year Flood Signal 6 Days in Advance; Enters Copernicus EMS Flood Service
items.summary: ECMWF's operationally deployed AIFL (AI for Floods) LSTM, trained on 18,588 river basins from the CARAVAN dataset, detects a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance — as demonstrated during Storm Henk (Belgium, January 2024). The deployment within Copernicus Emergency Management Service provides global flood early warning capability directly relevant to the current Pakistan, Nepal, and Southeast Asia flooding emergencies.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.25835: AI Weather Models “Missing the Butterfly” Traced to Training-Data Coarse-Graining — Butterfly Effect and Accurate Backcasting Both Explained by Same Root Cause
items.summary: A paper from the LMU Munich/ECMWF group identifies a unified root cause for two puzzling behaviors of AI weather prediction models: failure to simulate the butterfly effect and the surprising ability to skillfully backcast. The explanation is training-data coarse-graining, which removes fast, small-scale modes and creates a temporally smoothed training distribution. When coarse-graining is progressively reduced, the arrow of time and butterfly-effect sensitivity re-emerge. The finding has direct consequence for how AIWP benchmark accuracy should be interpreted — some advantage may reflect temporal smoothing rather than genuine dynamical skill.

items.title: Artemis London 2026: Cat Bond and ILS Market Well-Positioned for Disciplined Growth; AFME Calls for ILS to Back Climate Policies; 220 Attendees, 120+ Organizations; Innovations in London Bridge Cat Bonds and LoC Capital Stacks Discussed
items.body_html: The Artemis London 2026 conference on September 1 convened approximately 220 attendees representing more than 120 organizations from across the insurance-linked securities ecosystem, including ILS specialists, (re)insurance buyers, investors, fund managers, and specialist service providers. Speakers highlighted discipline in the catastrophe bond market and expected continued growth, with discussions covering catastrophe bonds issued under the London Bridge structure and the use of Letters of Credit to optimize capital stacks. The Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME) called for the use of insurance-linked securities and catastrophe bonds as an effective mechanism for insurers to access new capital to back climate-related policies — directly relevant as the Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report, released the same day, put average annual insured losses at a record $171 billion. The convergence of the ILS market growth discussion with the Verisk benchmark revision, Hurricane Lowell's developing Hawaii threat, and the ongoing Nepal-Tibet disaster underscores the direct line from extreme weather events under Super El Niño to capital markets.

items.title: Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report: Industry Should Prepare for $171 Billion in Average Annual Insured Losses — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; US Accounts for $117B (68%) of Global AAL; 100-Year Loss at $477B; Highest Estimate Verisk Has Ever Reported
items.body_html: Verisk released its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report on September 1, calculating that the insurance industry should be prepared to absorb $171 billion in insured catastrophe losses on an average annual basis — up $19 billion from its prior-year estimate and the highest average annual loss (AAL) figure Verisk has ever published. Of the $171 billion global insured AAL, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States; the 100-year return-period scenario yields $477 billion in aggregate insured losses, and the 250-year scenario reaches $606 billion. A companion release covers Europe: Europe carries $110 billion in expected annual economic catastrophe losses, of which only about $24 billion is currently insured — a protection gap of roughly 78%. Severe thunderstorm accounts for 40% of modelled insured catastrophe risk, followed by tropical cyclone (27%), earthquake (10%), winter storm (9%), flood (7%), and wildfire (6%).
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / Verisk / Insurance Journal

items.title: Redstone Closes €25 Million First Tranche of Blue Economy Decarbonization Fund — Targeting Maritime Sector Carbon Reduction, Ocean Asset Security, and Coastal Infrastructure Resilience
items.body_html: Berlin- and Helsinki-based fund manager Redstone closed the first tranche of its blue economy decarbonization fund at €25 million during the week of August 28, targeting investments in technologies to decarbonize maritime sectors, secure ocean-based assets, and build resilient coastal infrastructure. The fund addresses a sector responsible for approximately 2.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Alternative fuels (ammonia, methanol, green hydrogen), hull efficiency technologies, and port electrification represent core investment themes. The first close reflects growing investor interest in maritime decarbonization as the IMO’s strengthened 2050 net-zero shipping target creates regulatory pull for clean propulsion.

items.title: BlocPower Shuts Down and Liquidates — Community Clean Energy Electrification Platform Winds Down After 14 Years; Returns Capital to Investors
items.body_html: BlocPower, the community-focused clean energy company that electrified buildings in low-income urban neighborhoods by replacing gas heating and cooling systems with electric heat pumps and solar, is shutting down and liquidating its assets, returning remaining capital to investors. BlocPower had operated since 2012, achieving significant attention for its mission of decarbonizing community buildings in underserved neighborhoods across New York City and other markets. The closure is a notable setback for impact-oriented community climate tech and underscores the structural challenges facing mission-driven platforms trying to deploy clean energy in underserved markets at scale.

items.title: RFC Power Closes £10 Million Series A and Rebrands as Certain Energy — British Business Bank Leads; Centrica Energy, Ceres Power, and Temasek Trust C3H Participate; Manganese Flow Battery LDES Platform Targets Grid-Scale Deployment
items.body_html: RFC Power, an Imperial College London spin-off developing manganese-electrolyte flow batteries for long-duration energy storage, closed a £10 million ($12.7 million) Series A on August 26 and simultaneously rebranded as Certain Energy. The round was led by the British Business Bank, which contributed £3.5 million, with participation from Centrica Energy, Ceres Power Holdings, and Temasek Trust’s Catalytic Capital for Climate and Health (C3H). Certain Energy’s flow battery uses a manganese electrolyte and enables storage from hours to days without chemistry changes, targeting grid-connected MWh-class demonstration in India.
items.source_html: Renewable Energy Magazine / Solar Power Portal
